entries.snippet: Kenya's Health Minister Aden Duale was found in contempt of court on Monday for failing to halt the construction of an Ebola quarantine facility intended for Americans, despite existing court orders.

entries.snippet: Authorities in South Sudan on Monday set the date of Dec. 22 for the country's first general election since independence in 2011.

entries.snippet: The U.S. military has conducted another strike Sunday against a boat accused of smuggling drugs in the Caribbean on Sunday, immediately killing two people and leaving six survivors amid an ongoing campaign against alleged traffickers in Latin America.

entries.title: Judge says roommate of Charlie Kirk murder suspect won't testify in person at preliminary hearing
entries.snippet: The Utah judge in the murder case of Charlie Kirk's killing has denied a defense request to force Tyler Robinson's former roommate to testify in person during the preliminary hearing, saying that the credibility of any testimony can be challenged later if the case goes to trial.

entries.title: Lionel Messi breaks World Cup scoring record with his 17th and 18th goals in Argentina win
entries.snippet: Lionel Messi broke the World Cup scoring record with his 17th goal and then added an 18th in stoppage time in defending champion Argentina's 2-0 win over Austria on Monday.

entries.title: Merlin the duck steals the spotlight at President Sheinbaum's news briefing
entries.snippet: Wearing the green jersey of Mexico's national soccer team and a FIFA tie, he waddled into the room ahead of President Claudia Sheinbaum, took a seat facing reporters and quickly became the star of her Monday morning news briefing.

entries.title: China hits back at U.S. sanctions on tech giants, restricting its exports to American defense firms
entries.snippet: China on Monday announced sanctions on 10 American military-related companies in response to a recent U.S. move that bars some leading Chinese tech companies from defense contracts.

entries.title: Ukraine and Russia exchange deadly strikes, with at least 1 child killed in Sumy
entries.snippet: A Russian drone strike on the city of Sumy in northeastern Ukraine killed three members of the same family, including a 13-year-old boy, while a Ukrainian strike on a Russian industrial plant killed five people, officials said Monday.

entries.title: Staggering amounts of fentanyl hit streets as DEA watched and took no action, records show
entries.snippet: According to current and former DEA agents and records reviewed by The Associated Press, the U.S. Drug Enforcement Administration allowed hundreds of thousands of fentanyl pills to hit the streets of New Mexico from 2023 to 2025.

entries.title: Meet Andy Burnham, Britain’s likely next prime minister
entries.snippet: Now that British Prime Minister Keir Starmer announced his resignation, all eyes are on Andy Burnham. The former mayor of Manchester is seen as the favorite to succeed Starmer to lead the United Kingdom.

entries.title: Europe sizzles under heat wave with little relief in sight
entries.snippet: Germany, France, the UK and other European countries are experiencing extreme heat, with cooler weather not expected until the weekend. Several deaths were reported in France, including two children. DW has the latest.

entries.title: Germany's pension plans draw praise and outrage
entries.snippet: A 30-point plan to reform Germany's pension system has drawn praise and criticism in almost equal measure. Centrist politicians have called it a good compromise, opposition parties on the left and right are unhappy.

entries.title: Fact check: AI fakes around the World Cup spread political narratives
entries.snippet: Keir Starmer in a Croatia jersey. An Iranian protest against a US strike. Calls to arrest Brazil's President Lula. Adolf Hitler in the German fan section — all supposedly seen at the World Cup. But none of it is real.

entries.title: Germany and UK rebuilding ties 10 years after Brexit vote
entries.snippet: Ten years after the referendum, the two countries are strengthening their ties once again. The stability of these ties is now being put to the test with Keir Starmer to be replaced as prime minister.

entries.title: Iran-US talks to end war beset by tension, mistrust
entries.snippet: While both sides claim "encouraging progress," experts say there's a long way to go to turn the shaky diplomatic framework into a durable agreement.

entries.title: US-Iran deal: Pakistan's diplomatic masterstroke?
entries.snippet: By stepping in as mediator in the Iran war, Pakistan has managed to elevate its status from a regional player to a global diplomatic stakeholder — with a little help from China and its friends in the Gulf.

entries.title: Why is Bulgaria threatening to veto EU's Russia sanctions?
entries.snippet: Bulgarian PM Rumen Radev has vowed to veto the EU's latest sanctions against Russia because they include Russian Orthodox Patriarch Kirill and former Lukoil president Vagit Alekperov. What's behind his opposition?

entries.title: How inflation undermines Nigeria's sugar tax
entries.snippet: Nigeria's sugary drinks tax was meant to stop rising diabetes rates, but soaring inflation has eroded its impact. Experts say the levy is too small to change behavior and urge higher rates and reforms.

entries.title: 75 years of Germany's Goethe-Institut
entries.snippet: For 75 years, the Goethe-Institut has stood for cultural exchange, education and partnerships around the globe — even under challenging political conditions.

entries.title: The man who knew, but didn't say: Alan Greenspan (1926-2026)
entries.snippet: Alan Greenspan’s reputation as head of the US Federal Reserve was legendary — not least because of his reputation for convoluted statements. However, the 2008/9 financial crisis took a toll on his standing.

entries.title: Former US Fed chair Alan Greenspan dies aged 100
entries.snippet: Alan Greenspan oversaw the US Federal Reserve for nearly two decades from 1987 until 2006. Critics argue that his policies contributed to the Global Financial Crisis of 2008.

entries.title: Germany's Left Party is dreaming big
entries.snippet: The socialist Left Party has seen its membership soar and is especially popular with young female voters. Could it soon come to power in the city state of Berlin?

entries.title: US waives Iran oil sanctions citing progress in talks
entries.snippet: US officials have cited ongoing negotiations on allowing nuclear inspections and opening the Strait of Hormuz in pausing sanctions for 60 days. JD Vance said a "foundation" is in place for a final deal.

entries.title: India news: Millions of students turn up for NEET retest
entries.snippet: More than 2 million students appeared for the high-stakes NEET medical entrance exam amid high security after a question paper leak fiasco.

entries.title: UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer announces resignation
entries.snippet: In an emotional speech at 10 Downing Street, Keir Starmer said he will step down after days of mounting pressure and speculation over his future. It comes as leadership contender Andy Burnham returns to parliament.

entries.title: How TikTok-style videos keep human brains hooked on content
entries.snippet: TikTok, Instagram and YouTube clips are designed to overwhelm the brain's pleasure circuitry and keep people watching. Researchers say short-form videos may only be the start when it comes to harvesting human attention.

entries.title: Germany news: Could heatwave temperatures hit 40°C?
entries.snippet: Germany is in the grip of an intense heatwave, with experts predicting extreme temperatures in some regions. Chancellor Friedrich Merz insists he can handle the heat and is not bothered by personal insults.

entries.title: US-Iran talks end in Switzerland, mediators say
entries.snippet: According to mediators from Qatar and Pakistan, the talks between United States and Iranian officials in Switzerland have ended with both sides agreeing on a roadmap. Technical talks will continue.
